chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma Isma'il ibn Marar and others, from Yunus.

Regarding an Umm Walad (concubine who bore her master a child) who has no children of her own, when her child died and her master died without freeing her: Is it permissible for anyone to marry her? He said: 'No, she is a slave; it is not permissible for anyone to marry her except through manumission by the heirs. If she has a child, and there is no debt on the deceased, she belongs to the child. And when the child possesses her, she has become free by the possession of her child. If there are partners (in ownership), she has become free from the share of her child, and the remainder of her price is sought out (paid to the other partners).'

key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine who bore her master a child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying an Umm Walad after her master's death if he did not free her?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the posthumous status of an *Umm Walad* who has not yet been freed, establishing that she remains a slave property until her heirs execute her manumission. It highlights the Shia juristic view that if she bore a child, that child inherits her, and her freedom is secured through the child's share of the estate, with any remaining cost covered by the heirs. This ruling underscores the principle that manumission is an obligation on the estate rather than an immediate automatic freedom upon the master's death.
